title: Register Subroutine Run
statement: Let $A$ be a register program, let $q,r$ be distinct registers, and suppose its instructions at states $l,l_1,l_2$ are respectively: branch to $l_x$ when register $q$ is zero (with the other branch to $l_1$), decrement $q$ and go to $l_2$, then decrement $r$ and return to $l$. For every $k\in\mathbb N$ and register valuation $v$ with $v(q)=k$ and every register value at most $B$, there is a finite run from state $l$ to state $l_x$ that satisfies the guard requiring the program's side conditions and every register value to be at most $B$ at each earlier step. The final valuation sets $q$ to $0$, decreases $r$ by $k$ using truncated subtraction, and leaves all other registers unchanged; the final result is unset.
hypotheses_covered: instruction at $l$ is the specified zero test
instruction at $l_1$ decrements $q$ and goes to $l_2$
instruction at $l_2$ decrements $r$ and returns to $l$
all initial register values are at most $B$
